trace: I am looking at PLTR on the daily chart for oscillator divergences over the past three months. The most significant finding is a classic bearish divergence that ran across both MACD and RSI. Price formed a higher high at $25.80 roughly 18 days ago compared to a prior peak at $24.50 about 45 days earlier. Yet the MACD line peaked at +0.65 on the second top versus +0.88 on the first, a clear lower high in momentum. The RSI told the same story: at the $24.50 peak the RSI hit 72.1, overbought territory, but at the higher price of $25.80 it only reached 66.8. That failure to confirm the new price high is textbook bearish divergence and is exactly the kind of signal that often precedes a correction. The MACD has since crossed below its signal line nine sessions ago, with the current reading sitting at -0.28 against a signal of -0.21. RSI has dropped to 44.2, below the neutral 50 level. Price has broken below its 20-day EMA at $24.10 and the 50-day EMA at $23.55, both of which are now acting as dynamic resistance. The 200-day EMA at $19.80 remains intact, so the long-term trend is not broken. Short-term, the picture is bearish. I would watch for price to test the 38.2% Fibonacci retracement at $21.90 and horizontal support at $22.50 as the most probable pullback targets. A high-volume reversal candle back above the 20-day EMA would be the signal to abandon the bearish thesis and reconsider.

Looking at PLTR daily for bearish divergence across RSI, MACD, and MFI. The setup is fairly clear. Price hit $25.50 last week, a higher high versus $24.75 three weeks prior. The MACD line peaked at +0.68 on the recent high but had reached +0.85 at the prior, lower price peak. That is a lower high in momentum against a higher high in price, classic Class A bearish divergence. RSI confirmed the same pattern: the lower price high at $24.75 saw RSI peak at 74.8 but the higher price high at $25.50 only produced an RSI of 69.5. Buying pressure is measurably weakening. A bearish MACD crossover occurred two sessions ago, bringing the histogram into negative territory for the first time in weeks. RSI has dropped to 58.2 from overbought. Price is now trading just above the 20-day EMA at $24.10, which is the first meaningful support. The 50-day EMA at $22.80 and 200-day EMA at $19.50 are both still rising and in bullish alignment, which means this is likely a pullback within an uptrend rather than a full reversal. The divergence is a short-term warning, not a death knell. The rising wedge forming over the past month adds a bearish tilt. A break below the wedge's lower trendline near $24.00 on elevated volume would be the trigger for a short trade targeting the 50-day EMA around $22.80.

Shopify SHOP is showing a complex technical setup that centers on a large Head and Shoulders top pattern forming over the past six months. The left shoulder peaked near $80, the head reached around $88, and the right shoulder is struggling under $68 to $70 resistance. The neckline sits near $60.00, and a decisive close below it on increased volume would confirm the pattern and project a measured move to roughly $32 based on the height of the formation. The stock is already in a structurally weak position: price at $62.50 is below the 20-EMA at $64.80, the 50-EMA at $68.90, and the 200-SMA at $75.40. A Death Cross occurred three months ago. MACD is negative with the line at -1.85 below the signal at -1.50, and RSI sits at 41.2, bearish but showing a potential hidden bullish divergence as the indicator made a higher low while price made a slightly lower low. That divergence is worth watching. ATR has compressed to $2.15 from a six-month average of $3.50, and Bollinger Bands are contracting, with width at the 22nd percentile of its one-year range. The ADX at 28.1 confirms a moderately strong bearish trend, with minus-DI at 29.5 dominating plus-DI at 15.2. The compression in volatility combined with the overhead resistance from all major moving averages and the Head and Shoulders neckline nearby makes this a high-stakes setup. Volume confirmation on a neckline break will be critical.

Reviewing Costco COST for bearish divergence on RSI. The signal is real and the corroborating evidence is strong. Price posted a new all-time high at $870.75 but the RSI peaked at only 71.3, meaningfully below the 78.2 reading seen during the prior price high. That divergence across two peaks is the primary bearish signal. MACD echoes it: price hit the new high but the MACD line formed a lower high at +10.80 versus the prior peak of +11.20, and a bearish crossover occurred three sessions ago with the histogram now printing at -0.75. RSI has since slid to 62.5 from 78.2 just eight sessions ago. The Stochastic at 55.8 is falling sharply from overbought territory, and Williams percent-R at -35.2 has moved out of the overbought zone. The technical picture is starting to look fatigued at these highs. Price is still 3.1 percent above the 20-day EMA at $840.10, and that EMA has served as dynamic support for the past 45 sessions. A close below it would be the first meaningful technical warning. Bollinger Band width is at the 85th percentile, indicating extended conditions. ADX remains high at 48.5 but has just begun ticking down. No classic reversal pattern like a head and shoulders has formed yet, but the rounding action near the highs is notable. Given the long-term uptrend is intact, this setup favors a pullback toward $840 rather than a full reversal, unless the 50-day EMA at $795.50 fails.

ROKU has made a multi-week high at $72.50 while multiple oscillators are refusing to confirm. This is a textbook multi-indicator bearish divergence setup. On the MACD, the recent high at $72.50 produced a line reading of +1.25, well below the +1.88 recorded when price was at $70.10 ten sessions ago. A bearish MACD crossover occurred two sessions ago. The RSI paints the same picture: at $70.10 RSI hit 74.2, but at the higher price of $72.50 it only reached 62.5. The Stochastic oscillator adds a third confirming voice, reading 75.8 on the latest peak versus 92.1 on the prior one. Three oscillators all showing lower highs against a higher price high is a strong bearish divergence signal. Price has been touching the upper Bollinger Band at $73.10 but failing to close above it. The rising wedge pattern between $63.00 and $72.50 is converging, with lower wedge support currently near $69.00. ADX at 35.2 shows a strong trend but has just started ticking down from 38. ATR at $3.15 is elevated. A potential short setup would trigger on a break below the rising wedge support at $69.00, with the 20-day EMA at $67.80 as the first target and the prior swing low at $66.50 as a secondary. Stop above the recent high at $72.50. The bearish divergence across three independent oscillators combined with wedge breakdown confirmation gives this setup meaningful credibility.

PLTR has been consolidating for roughly five months and the technical picture is defined by a symmetrical triangle pattern. The upper trendline connects a series of lower highs and currently sits near $25.50, while the lower trendline connects higher lows near $22.50. The apex is approaching in mid-to-late July, implying a breakout decision is imminent within two to four weeks. Inside this pattern, the technical indicators are neutral to slightly constructive. MACD is barely positive with the line at +0.45 above the signal at +0.41, but the histogram is only +0.04, suggesting momentum is building slowly. RSI at 55.2 is moving up from a recent low of 42 and is trending in the right direction, though no divergence of note is present. The Bollinger Band squeeze is the standout observation: band width at 10.5 percent of price is well below the one-year average, signaling that a significant move is being coiled. ADX at 14.8 confirms the absence of a trend. Volume has been declining through the pattern, falling 30 percent below the three-month average in recent weeks, which is normal behavior for a valid symmetrical triangle. OBV has been drifting slightly lower, which is a mild caution flag. The 200-day EMA at $20.10 provides a long-term floor. A bullish breakout above $25.50 on volume at least 50 percent above average would target the prior major high at $27.50 and then the psychological $30.00 level. A breakdown below $22.50 targets the 200-day EMA zone around $20.50.

ROKU has rallied sharply and now shows bearish divergences across three oscillators simultaneously on the daily chart. Price hit $98.50 recently while the MACD peaked at +4.10 five days earlier and has since declined to +3.45, a clear lower high in momentum against a new price high. RSI peaked at 74.8 one week ago but has already fallen to 66.2 by the time price reached the new high, another non-confirmation. The Stochastic at 84.5 is printing overbought and has made a bearish crossover with percent-K falling below percent-D in the overbought zone. CCI came off a peak of +210 and is now at +130 with a lower high. Williams percent-R is at -15.8 and rolling over. The convergence of bearish signals across MACD, RSI, Stochastic, CCI, and Williams all simultaneously failing to confirm the price high strengthens the overall case considerably. Price tagged the upper Bollinger Band at $99.10 yesterday but closed lower. A potential double top is forming with peaks at $97.80 and $98.50, with the neckline at the recent swing low of $88.50. Price is 8.5 percent above the 20-EMA at $90.32 and 15.2 percent above the 50-EMA, suggesting significant mean-reversion risk. The 200-day EMA at $78.34 remains a major long-term support. ATR at $4.75 is elevated, meaning any reversal could move quickly. A break below the double top neckline at $88.50 would confirm the pattern and project a target near $78.50.

AbbVie ABBV is testing six-month highs at $172.50 and the divergence case across RSI, MACD, and Stochastic is clear and consistent. On MACD, the prior price high at $170.00 three weeks ago corresponded with a MACD peak of +2.88, but today's higher price high at $172.50 only produced a MACD reading of +1.90. The MACD line has already crossed below its signal, generating the bearish crossover two sessions ago. RSI shows the same story even more starkly: the lower price high at $170.00 produced an RSI peak of 78.2, while the higher price high at $172.50 only reached 66.5. That is a drop of nearly 12 RSI points on a higher price, a strong signal of weakening buying pressure. The Stochastic confirms with a reading of 85.1 on the current peak versus 94.3 at the prior one. Price is touching the upper Bollinger Band at $172.80 but band width is not expanding on this new high, indicating lack of follow-through momentum. The rising wedge pattern over the past month reinforces the bearish interpretation. ADX at 33.4 shows a strong trend but is starting to flatten. Immediate support is the wedge's lower trendline near $167.50 and the 20-day EMA at $165.07. The 38.2 percent Fibonacci retracement of the recent swing from $155.00 to $172.50 sits at $165.80, closely aligned with the 20-day EMA, making that zone the primary pullback target on a confirmed wedge breakdown.

The most important technical finding for PLTR from a volume perspective is an OBV divergence that conflicts with the price structure. While price has been making higher lows within a symmetrical triangle over the past two months, the OBV line has been making lower lows. Price is bullishly positioned within the triangle but money flow is quietly telling a different story. This is a subtle but meaningful warning. A volume spike five weeks ago at 120 million shares, which was 2.6 times the average, occurred on a sharp down day. Price recovered quickly, but that kind of spike on a down day often signals distribution by large holders. The consolidation since then shows normal volume decline to 45 million shares average, which is expected in a triangle pattern. The symmetrical triangle itself has an upper trendline near $26.75 and a lower trendline near $24.10, with the apex several weeks away. MACD at +0.45 above the signal +0.38 is constructive but weak, with the histogram barely positive at +0.07. RSI at 58.2 is neutral but has been making lower highs since peaking at 75 two months ago, itself a hint of underlying momentum weakness. ADX at 18.5 confirms a ranging, trendless environment. Given the OBV divergence and the distribution spike, I would want to see a breakout above $26.75 on heavy volume before trusting the upside. A breakdown below $24.10 with OBV confirming downward would validate the distribution interpretation.

AMD has built a symmetrical triangle over the past eight weeks that has all the classic characteristics of a high-probability breakout setup. The upper trendline connects the highs at $184 and $174, descending at roughly -$0.40 per day. The lower trendline connects the lows at $148 and $155, rising at approximately +$0.25 per day. These two lines converge at the apex around late July, meaning a breakout decision is likely within two to four weeks. The triangle's widest point measures $36, from $184 to $148. A bullish breakout above the upper trendline near $168 targets $204, while a bearish breakdown below the lower trendline near $158 targets $122. The internal indicators all confirm the consolidation thesis. Bollinger Band width at 0.08 is in the 12th percentile of its one-year range, a genuine volatility squeeze. ADX at 18.2 confirms the absence of trend. ATR has fallen 45 percent from $7.50 to $4.15. MACD at -0.85 is below zero but the histogram is contracting, hinting at potential stabilization. RSI at 48.5 is perfectly neutral. The 200-day EMA at $145.20 anchors long-term support and the 20-day EMA at $162.50 and 50-day EMA at $164.10 are converging and flat inside the triangle. Volume has been declining through the pattern as expected. A breakout on volume at least 50 percent above the 20-day average would provide the confirmation needed to trade the directional move with confidence.

PLTR is in a strong uptrend but momentum exhaustion is showing up across RSI, MACD, and Stochastic simultaneously, which raises the probability of a near-term pullback. Price made a higher high at $26.50 last week compared to $25.80 the week before. Yet the MACD line posted a lower high of +0.88 versus a prior peak of +1.15, and RSI peaked at only 69 at the new high compared to 78.5 at the lower prior price high. That multi-indicator bearish divergence is the core signal. MACD has since crossed below its signal line two sessions ago and the histogram has been declining for seven sessions from a peak of +0.25 to current negative territory. Stochastic fell from above 80 and made a bearish crossover four sessions ago, now at 55.4. CCI dropped from +190 to +85. Williams percent-R moved from overbought out to -38.0. All short-term momentum indicators are pointing the same direction. Price is now just above its 20-day EMA at $24.85, which is the first support to watch. The 50-day EMA at $23.10 is next. The longer-term structure remains bullish, with the 200-day EMA at $20.05 and the overall moving average stack in bullish alignment. ADX at 38.2 has peaked and is ticking down. The key variable for this pullback is volume. Volume on the past two up-days has been below the 20-day average, which is consistent with a weak final push. A high-volume surge to new highs would negate the divergence thesis entirely.

AMD is in a corrective phase but bullish divergences are forming across RSI, MACD, and Stochastic that suggest the selling pressure is becoming exhausted. The clearest signal is on RSI: price made a lower low at $145.60 last week compared to $150.20 three weeks earlier, but the RSI printed a higher low of 28.5 versus 25.1 at the prior trough. Higher RSI on a lower price low is the definition of classic bullish divergence and indicates sellers are losing strength. The MACD confirms this reading. The histogram posted a higher low at -4.20 versus -5.80 during the previous trough, and a bullish MACD crossover occurred four sessions ago below the zero line, with the histogram now positive and expanding to +0.55. The Stochastic crossed up from the oversold zone with percent-K above percent-D. A Bullish Engulfing candle formed at the $145.60 low, providing candlestick confirmation. The broader context is still bearish: price is below the 20-day EMA at $158.10 and the 50-day EMA at $169.50. The 200-day EMA at $151.20 is the key battleground, with price currently challenging it from below. Reclaiming the 200-day EMA is the critical near-term test. If price can close above it on volume, the inverse head and shoulders pattern that appears to be forming would gain credibility, with the right shoulder forming now and the neckline near $165.00. Failure at the 200-day EMA would reassert the bearish trend and potentially set up a death cross.

Salesforce CRM is showing a high-probability bearish reversal setup. A Class A bearish divergence on MACD is confirmed: price made a higher high at $315 two weeks ago while the MACD line peaked at +5.80, below its prior peak of +6.90 when price was at $305 a month earlier. The RSI corroborates with equal force: the $315 high produced an RSI of 65.1, well below the 74.3 reading at the prior and lower price high. A bearish MACD crossover occurred four sessions ago with the histogram now at -1.43 and expanding negatively. RSI has broken below the 50 neutral level, shifting sentiment from bullish to bearish. Price has just closed below the 20-day EMA at $302.50 for the first time in 25 sessions. A potential double top is forming with peaks at $305 and $315, with the neckline at $292. A shooting star at the $315 peak followed by three consecutive large red candles confirms distribution at the high. The 38.2 percent Fibonacci retracement of the $250 to $315 swing sits at $290.17, which nearly perfectly aligns with the 50-day EMA at $289.10 and the double top neckline, making that zone the highest-probability pullback target. CCI has crossed below -100, confirming a new bearish impulse. The longer-term trend is intact with the 200-day EMA at $255.40 still rising, so this is a medium-term correction within a longer uptrend, but the $289 to $292 zone is a reasonable short-selling target on a confirmed neckline break.

Caterpillar CAT has formed a double top with peaks at $362.00 and $368.50, and the bearish divergence across MACD, RSI, and Stochastic all confirm that the second top was built on weakening momentum. The MACD peaked at +3.10 on the recent high versus +5.50 at the prior high, a dramatic lower high in momentum. RSI peaked at 64.1 at $368.50 versus 72.3 at the lower prior high of $362.00 a month ago. The Stochastic also failed to make a new high alongside price. A bearish MACD crossover occurred four sessions ago, with the histogram negative and expanding at -1.25. RSI has just crossed below 50, signaling a shift from bullish to bearish momentum. Price closed below the 20-day EMA at $359.80 and is now trading at roughly $356 based on the context, threatening the 50-day EMA at $348.10. The double top neckline sits at $340.00, the trough between the two peaks. A confirmed break below that neckline would project a measured move to approximately $311.50. The shooting star at the $368.50 peak followed by bearish continuation candles confirms the technical picture. ADX at 28.9 peaked and is now falling, with minus-DI crossing above plus-DI. The 200-day EMA far below at $304.50 provides the ultimate long-term support. For a medium-term trade, I would target the 50-day EMA at $348.10 as an initial destination and the neckline at $340.00 as the secondary target, with a stop above the recent high.

Shopify SHOP is presenting a nuanced picture with a strong weekly bearish divergence that already played out and a nascent daily bullish divergence that is now forming a potential base. On the weekly chart, MACD made a lower high as price made a higher high from July to December, a classic multi-month bearish divergence that foreshadowed the subsequent 30 percent correction. That divergence has resolved to the downside and the move has already occurred. Now on the daily chart, a potential Class A bullish divergence is forming. Price made a lower low yesterday at $56.50 compared to $58.10 five days ago, but the RSI printed a higher low at 34.5 versus 31.2. The price is touching the lower Bollinger Band and multiple oscillators are deep in oversold territory: Stochastic at 22.1, CCI at -135, Williams percent-R at -88.4. A Death Cross on the daily chart confirmed eight sessions ago and price is below all key moving averages, so the primary trend is clearly bearish. The daily RSI divergence is therefore a counter-trend signal that argues for a bounce rather than a full reversal. Key resistance on any bounce would be the 200-day SMA at $59.50 followed by the 20-day EMA at $62.80. The long-legged doji candle yesterday at the lows adds to the bottoming evidence. I would treat any bounce to the $59 to $63 zone as a potential re-entry for shorts rather than a sustained reversal unless price can reclaim the 50-day EMA at $67.10 with volume.

Plug Power PLUG is a high-volatility energy stock deep in a downtrend, but bullish divergences are forming across MACD, RSI, and Stochastic that suggest the immediate selling pressure is fading. The most pronounced signal is on RSI: price made a lower low at $2.38 recently while the RSI printed a higher low of 28.1, compared to an RSI reading of 22.5 at the prior and higher price low of $2.60. That is a clear bullish divergence. MACD is also diverging: the MACD line made a higher low at -0.15 compared to -0.28 during the prior trough, while the histogram is ticking upward toward zero. Stochastic crossed up from oversold levels. Two bullish engulfing candles have formed at the recent low. Volume on the final down-leg was meaningfully lower than prior down-legs, supporting the thesis that selling is exhausting. The structural context is still bearish: price at $2.55 is below all key moving averages with the 20-day EMA at $2.85, 50-day EMA at $3.15, and 200-day SMA at $4.50. A Death Cross is firmly in place. ADX at 45.8 shows a very strong downtrend with minus-DI at 42.6 dominating plus-DI at 15.1. The falling wedge pattern that has been building adds a bullish tilt. ATR at $0.22 represents 8.6 percent of the stock price, so even small moves are significant in percentage terms. A bounce to the 20-day EMA at $2.85 is the immediate target with the 23.6 percent Fibonacci retracement of the $3.50 to $2.38 swing sitting at $2.64 as an initial test. A break below $2.38 on volume would invalidate the thesis.

ROKU rallied hard post-earnings and is now showing bearish divergence signals at key resistance. Price reached $98.50 two days ago, a new rally high. But the MACD peaked at +4.50 two weeks prior and only produced +3.95 at this new price high, a lower high in momentum. The RSI peaked at 78.5 during the initial surge but only reached 69.1 at the recent $98.50 high. That is a drop of nearly 10 RSI points at a higher price, a meaningful non-confirmation. A bearish MACD crossover occurred three sessions ago with the histogram now at -0.73 and expanding. RSI has since fallen to 58.2. A potential double top is forming with peaks at $98.10 and $98.50, separated by a trough at $90.50. A break below $90.50 would confirm the pattern and project a measured move to approximately $82.50. Price has also fallen from the upper Bollinger Band and is now below the middle band, testing the 20-day EMA at $91.50. Stochastic has crossed below its signal line from overbought territory. CCI has dropped from +210 to +85. ADX at 35.2 is starting to roll over from a peak of 42.1. The 50-day EMA at $82.10 and 200-day EMA at $75.40 are both rising, indicating the longer-term trend is intact. ATR at $4.85 is elevated and suggests any reversal from here could be sharp. The combination of double top formation, multi-indicator bearish divergence, and overbought oscillators rolling over makes this a high-credibility reversal setup targeting the $82 to $85 zone.

Block SQ has developed a compelling bullish divergence on the weekly chart that signals the prolonged downtrend may be turning. The core signal is on MACD: price printed a lower low at $38.90 in October 2023 compared to the prior trough of $51.34 in May 2023, but the MACD line formed a higher low at the October bottom. A bullish MACD crossover occurred four weeks ago, bringing the histogram positive. RSI tells an equally clear story: the May 2023 low at $51.34 produced an RSI of 25.1, while the deeper October 2023 low at $38.90 only pushed RSI to 28.5. Price made a lower low but RSI made a higher low. The Stochastic oscillator also shows the same higher low pattern at the October trough. All three oscillators are confirming each other across two major weekly lows, making this one of the stronger divergence setups I am reviewing. The weekly RSI has since moved to 55.2, recovering from deeply oversold conditions. Price is now challenging the 20-week EMA at $65.10, a critical short-term test. The 50-week SMA at $72.80 and 200-week SMA at $115.40 are well overhead. A double bottom pattern is potentially forming with the lows at $51.34 and $38.90, and confirmation would require a breakout above the intermediate peak between those lows at roughly $89.95. ADX at 35.1 is still high but beginning to curl down, indicating the prior downtrend is weakening. A confirmed weekly close above the 20-week EMA at $65.10 is the immediate bull trigger.

Exxon Mobil XOM is showing a potentially significant Head and Shoulders top forming on the weekly chart, which is the kind of pattern that, if confirmed, would represent a meaningful medium-term trend change. The left shoulder peaked around $112.20 between October and December 2023. The head formed between March and May 2024 with a peak at $120.70. The right shoulder is currently forming with price action consolidating in the $113 to $118 range. The neckline connecting the two pattern lows sits at approximately $100.50 to $101.00, which is a critical long-term support level. The weekly MACD crossed bearishly three weeks ago with the current line at +2.15 below the signal at +2.50, and the histogram has been negative for three consecutive weeks. RSI on the weekly has pulled back to 54.8 from a peak near 72 two months ago, and while not yet showing a dramatic divergence, the downward slope is notable. The weekly 20-day EMA at $113.50 is being tested now. The 50-week EMA at $108.90 and the 38.2 percent Fibonacci retracement of the October 2023 to April 2024 rally both converge in the $113 range, creating a meaningful support cluster. Volume during the head formation was high as expected, but the right shoulder is forming on declining volume, which is characteristic of a valid pattern. A confirmed weekly close below the neckline at $101.00 would project a measured move to approximately $81.30 based on the pattern's height.

Salesforce CRM is showing bearish divergences that align on both RSI and MACD, and the follow-through price action is beginning to confirm the signal. Price posted a higher high at $315 roughly 15 days ago while the MACD line peaked at +5.80 versus the prior peak of +7.10 at the lower price high. RSI peaked at 68.5 on the new high compared to 75.2 at the prior lower high, a classic case of momentum not confirming price. Both divergences are Class A, occurring at clearly defined price peaks. A bearish MACD crossover occurred four sessions ago with the histogram at -1.05 and expanding. RSI has since fallen below 50, now at 48.2, which marks a shift in the short-term trend balance from bullish to neutral/bearish. Price has just closed below the 20-day EMA at $305.50, the first such close in several weeks. The CCI at -95.7 is approaching the -100 level where many traders interpret a new bearish impulse as beginning. The minus-DI at 24.1 has crossed above the plus-DI at 22.8, a bearish DI crossover. For a 1 to 3 month trade, the 50-day EMA at $292.10 is the primary target, followed by the prior swing low at $298. If the primary uptrend line from the October low at $285 gives way, that would materially extend the bearish case. A stop above the $315 all-time high defines the risk. Risk-reward from current levels to the 50-day EMA is approximately 2 to 1, which is adequate for a trade of this duration.

AMD has posted a higher high at $184.92 against a weakening momentum backdrop, and the bearish divergence case is supported by both primary oscillators. On MACD, the price peak at $184.92 produced a MACD line of +5.21, below the +6.88 reading at the prior price high of $180.33 one month ago. The histogram has turned negative and is expanding. RSI peaked at 78.2 at the recent high versus 84.5 at the lower prior high, a drop of over 6 RSI points at a higher price. Two independent momentum indicators are both showing the same pattern of divergence, which increases confidence in the signal. A bearish MACD crossover occurred four sessions ago. RSI is now at 54.1 and has broken its two-month uptrend line. Price is testing the 20-day EMA at $172.50, which is the critical near-term support. A potential double top is forming with the two peaks at $180.33 and $184.92, with the confirmation neckline at the trough between them at $165.20. A break below $165.20 would confirm the pattern and project a measured move toward approximately $145. The 50-day EMA at $161.80 provides the next support below the neckline. ADX at 38.9 is still elevated but has started ticking down from 45. ATR at $5.80 means stops need to be placed thoughtfully. The longer-term trend is bullish with the 200-day EMA at $135.10, so this setup is best interpreted as a meaningful correction opportunity rather than a structural short. Target the 50-day EMA at $161.80 with a stop above the recent all-time high.

AMD is showing short-term bearish divergence signals that are being confirmed by weakening price action and the first break of the 20-day EMA in over a month. Price peaked at $184.92 ten days ago. At that peak, MACD was at +3.45 but had previously reached +4.12 at the prior lower price high. RSI reached only 68.2 at $184.92 versus 79.5 at the prior peak. Both oscillators made lower highs against the new price high. A bearish MACD crossover occurred four sessions ago. RSI is now at 48.5 and has crossed below 50 for the first time in weeks. Price has broken below the 20-day EMA at $175.50 and is now trading below the middle Bollinger Band at $176.10, which has become resistance. The lower Bollinger Band at $166.70 is the next potential support. Stochastic at 22.5 is approaching oversold territory. CCI at -115.8 is definitively in bearish territory. The 50-day EMA at $164.20 is the next significant support below current price. A potential double top pattern has the neckline at $168.00, and a confirmed close below that level would project to approximately $151 on a measured move basis. Volume on recent down-days has included a large bearish engulfing candle three sessions ago, showing conviction from sellers at these levels. The 200-day EMA at $135.80 confirms the primary trend is still upward, but in the short term the bears have taken control. ATR at $5.80 elevated, so stops above $175.50 and targets near $164.20 makes sense for a short-term trade.

AMD has made a new high at $184.92 while the RSI and MACD are both failing to confirm the move, establishing a classic bearish divergence. The MACD line peaked at +5.25 at $184.92 but had previously peaked at +6.10 when price was at $180.25 two weeks prior. RSI peaked at 74.1 at the new high versus 78.5 at the lower prior high.
